description: A fungal disease affecting cucurbits (cucumber, melon, squash, watermelon, pumpkin). Causes lesions on leaves, stems, and fruits, especially in warm, humid, rainy conditions. Can survive on seeds, soil, and plant debris, and spreads by rain, wind, tools, workers, and insects.
symptoms: Leaves: oily spots near veins, angular brown/red/black lesions, tissue death or drop
Stems and petioles: elongated, depressed, yellowish lesions, may produce black acervules under humid conditions
Fruits: circular, sunken brown lesions, may ooze red gummy exudate on melon; gelatinous salmon-colored spores on watermelon
favorable_conditions: Soil and crop debris harboring pathogen
management: Destroy infected plants and crop debris
Rotate cucurbits with non-host crops for 2–3 seasons
Prune plants to increase airflow and reduce humidity
Avoid overhead irrigation and work when plants are wet
biological_control: Trichoderma harzianum: competes with pathogen, inhibits growth up to 72%
Bacillus subtilis: bio-pesticide to prevent pathogen establishment
Plant extracts: horsetail decoction, garlic or neem extracts inhibit fungal growth
Adjust pH on leaf surface with bicarbonate to reduce fungus development
chemical_control: Apply early morning or late evening
Ensure proper coverage, absorbed in 2 hours
Limit to one application per season or rotate with other fungicides
Follow safety precautions (gants, masque, lunettes) and pre-harvest interval
prevention: Remove volunteer crops and crop debris
Maintain good field sanitation and air circulation
Implement crop rotation with cereals, legumes, or brassicas
